harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Archive mailbox cutover completed. Node1 runs persistent TLS IMAP on RHEL 9.8 with Dovecot 2.3.16. Node2 authenticates as the dedicated archive account and retrieves both messages with matching Message-IDs, bodies, and read/unread state. The staged source remains intact. Both nodes were rebooted individually and fully reverified.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled the RHEL-supported Dovecot package without changing the operating-system release or kernel.
Created the dedicated archive account with a node-generated demonstration password.
Copied the staged messages into a separate working Maildir and applied the Seen flag only to one.eml.
Configured persistent SELinux labeling and firewall access for TLS IMAP.
Verified the mailbox remotely from node2 before and after both node reboots.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, proving changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Working IMAP service on node1 using legacy-platform-compatible software
evidence.summary: Dovecot 2.3.16 was installed from RHEL 9 repositories and is enabled, active, listening on IMAPS, and allowed through the firewall; RHEL 9.8 and the original kernel remain installed.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated archive account and demonstration password
evidence.summary: The dedicated non-login archive account exists, and node2 successfully authenticated using its separately generated demonstration credential.

evidence.requirement: Both messages preserve Message-ID, body, and read/unread state
evidence.summary: Remote read-only IMAP retrieval shows <one@branch.test> with body 'Shipment arrived.' and Seen state, plus <two@branch.test> with body 'Shipment departed.' and no Seen flag. Mailbox status confirms two messages and one unseen.

evidence.requirement: The only staged source remains intact
evidence.summary: Initial and final source hashes are unchanged, and each working message has the same SHA-256 hash as its staged original.

Healthy baseline boot ID 3aee314b-4dfc-4c3a-90f6-2b07c621eaa0 was captured; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to 0efdf2e8-fa5e-4ca3-922a-055a6910303f; service, firewall, SELinux context, source, mailbox data, and remote retrieval recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 377b5195-7fea-4219-a67b-044ef3f7ab99 was captured; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to 370e88f5-2f6c-4828-a5c0-bc7e055f32a9; networking, authentication, retrieval, message content, and flags recovered.
